before.name: Population served by water systems with no health-based violations
before.source: New York State Department of Health, 2025 Annual Report of Public Water Supply Violations — New York City system report (sourced from SDWIS/State, the state instance of EPA's Safe Drinking Water Information System)

scoring.worked_math: level_pct = (target − value) ⁄ scale × 100 = (100 − 100) ⁄ 100 × 100 = 0.0 (at the boundary — fully compliant, no shortfall)

after.name: Population served by water systems with no health-based violations
after.source: NYSDOH2025 annual compliance report; DEP2025 drinking-water report; EPA ECHO current system record
after.geography: NYC drinking-water system — shared citywide context
after.notes: NYSDOH says no violations were entered in SDWIS/State for 2025, and DEP reports meeting all drinking-water standards in 2025. EPA ECHO concurrently lists treatment-technique violation #20170201, beginning February 1, 2017, as Addressed under a May 15, 2019 federal consent decree; recent quarters remain Violation-Addressed. These describe different annual and historical compliance constructs. Neither proves that zero residents had safe tap water. The configured population-with-no-health-based-violations indicator cannot be scored consistently until the reporting period and treatment of addressed historical violations are resolved. Borough evidence refers to the shared NYC system.
